source_quote: Either party may terminate a Partner Agreement for convenience, for any reason, by providing at least 30 days' prior written notice to the other party. No early-termination fee or compensation is payable by either party. During the notice period, both parties continue to perform their existing obligations through the effective date of termination.

_calibration: §31.3 states 'at least 30 days' — the floor, so a longer partner-facing notice is not a deviation and a shorter one is. CONVENIENCE-NOTICE-MSA-001's own _calibration already cites this section ('a partner agreement's at least 30 days prior written notice (§31.3) — MATCH'), so the two agree by construction; they stay separate standards because they govern different document types.

The 'no early-termination fee' limb of §31.3 is a PRESENCE question, not a notice period, and is deliberately NOT folded into this NUMERIC_COMPARISON standard — one standard, one measurable position (45B). It is unmeasured until a separate standard is ratified for it.
Negative patterns keep for-cause termination (a cure-period question) out of this standard's mapping.
